1	import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2).
5	 * `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2: "inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and
6	 * the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details
7	 * gap widens 12 -> 16px." (the gap widening is `ZimmCartItem`'s own `hasError` resolution prop —
8	 * see product-item.css.ts — not this recipe's concern; this file owns only the message's own
9	 * type/colour.)
10	 *
11	 * Single visual node, no independent per-part state — `defineStyleConfig` + `useStyleConfig(...,
12	 * {variant})` (ZimmNavItem's / ZimmWishlistBadge's pattern) applies directly here, rather than
13	 * ZimmQuantityStepper's function-form `baseStyle` (which exists there because that recipe has
14	 * multiple PARTS needing independent values from one shared boolean, not a single Chakra-native
15	 * `variant` switch).
16	 *
17	 * --- Typography: regular weight is a DELIBERATE override, on a DIFFERENT Figma node than the
18	 * one commit 5 (SFCC-270) corrected — read both before touching either ---
19	 * `textStyle: 'caption'` supplies the correct 12px size / 18px line-height pair, but this
20	 * codebase's `caption` textStyle (theme/foundation/typography.ts) is MEDIUM-weight
21	 * (`fontWeight: fontWeights.medium`) — that is exactly right for Figma's OTHER caption node,
22	 * `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart-item colour+size line — see
23	 * item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84, which deliberately keeps `caption` with NO fontWeight
24	 * override for that reason, having removed an earlier, backwards override). THIS element is
25	 * Figma's plain, un-strong `Default/Caption` node, which is REGULAR-weight per the session-notes
26	 * citation above — the opposite correction, on a different string, elsewhere in the same design
27	 * file. `fontWeight` is therefore set explicitly below to override the textStyle-expanded medium
28	 * value back down to regular — the same "a direct CSS prop applied after the textStyle expansion
29	 * wins in Chakra's style pipeline" mechanism zimmButton.css.ts's `sizes.lg`/`sizes.sm` already
30	 * documents and relies on for the identical reason.
31	 *
32	 * `width: 'full'` reproduces Figma's own "w-full" annotation for this element explicitly, rather
33	 * than relying on this node's flex/stack parent to stretch it by default.
34	 *
35	 * No low-stock variant: a separate requirement explicitly forbids low-stock messaging at the
36	 * cart level (SFCC-795 §11.2 build decisions) — the variants map below only ever has the two
37	 * keys `error`/`warning`; do not add a third.
38	 */
39	const baseStyle = {
40	  textStyle: 'caption',
41	  fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
42	  width: 'full',
43	};
44	
45	const variants = {
46	  // Figma `text/error` #9c0000 -> status.error (session-notes.md §11.10(6) colour audit).
47	  error: {
48	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)',
49	  },
50	  // Figma `text/muted` / `text/subtlest` #969696 -> both collapse onto this one token, no
51	  // ambiguity in this codebase's own set (session-notes.md §11.10(6)).
52	  //
53	  // Max-quantity messaging ("Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") uses THIS variant,
54	  // not `error` — even though its own requirement/AC text uses the word "error" to describe it.
55	  // That word is describing "user-facing feedback" in the requirement's own vocabulary, not
56	  // asserting the error SEVERITY tier: the actual Figma design and that story's own AC agree the
57	  // rendered treatment is grey/warning, not red/error. Deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation,
58	  // settled at this build's planning gate — not a mistake, and not to be "corrected" back to
59	  // `error` by a future reader matching the word alone.
60	  warning: {
61	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)',
62	  },
63	};
64	
65	export const ZimmInlineMessage = defineStyleConfig({
66	  baseStyle,
67	  variants,
68	});

111	type ProductItemProps = {
112	  product: SfccProduct;
113	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
114	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
115	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
116	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
117	  /**
118	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
119	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
120	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
121	   */
122	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;

124	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
125	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;

132	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
133	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a

154	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
155	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
156	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
157	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
158	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
159	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
160	 */
161	const ProductItem = ({
162	  product,
163	  primaryAction,
164	  secondaryActions,
165	  deliveryActions,
166	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
167	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
168	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
169	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
170	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
171	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
172	  showLoading = false,
173	  containerStyles = {},
174	  isRemoving = false,
175	  pickupInStore = false,
176	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
177	  message,
178	}: ProductItemProps) => {
179	  const { stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
180	    product,
181	    false,
182	    false,
183	    pickupInStore,
184	  );
185	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
186	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
187	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
188	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
189	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
190	  return (
191	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
192	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
193	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
194	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
195	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">

197	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
198	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
199	                <Stack spacing={1}>
200	                  <CartItemVariantName />
201	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
202	                  <HideOnDesktop>
203	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
204	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
205	                    </Box>
206	                  </HideOnDesktop>
207	                </Stack>
208	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
209	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
210	                )}
211	              </Flex>
212	
213	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
214	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
215	              )}
216	
217	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
218	                <Stack spacing={1}>
219	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
220	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
221	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
222	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />

224	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
225	                        product={product}
226	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
227	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
228	                        quantity={quantity}
229	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
230	                      />
231	                    ))}
232	                </Stack>
233	                <Stack>
234	                  <HideOnMobile>
235	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
236	                  </HideOnMobile>
237	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
238	                </Stack>
239	              </Flex>
240	
241	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
242	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
243	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
244	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
245	
246	              <Box>
247	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
248	                  <Fade in={true}>
249	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
250	                      {inventoryMessage}
251	                    </Text>
252	                  </Fade>
253	                )}
254	              </Box>
255	
256	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
257	            </Stack>
258	          </Flex>
259	
260	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
261	            <HideOnDesktop>
262	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
263	            </HideOnDesktop>
264	          )}
265	        </Stack>
266	      </ItemVariantProvider>
267	    </Box>
268	  );
269	};

11	 * focused, filled}`, so a differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch
12	 * walked by that guard.

18	/**
19	 * Co-located recipe for the cart line-item shell (overrides/app/components/product-item).
20	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2) — restyles the copy-first port to the Figma-sourced cart-item spec.
21	 *
22	 * Parts:
23	 *   - `row` — the image + item-details row. Figma: gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align
24	 *     centre desktop / start mobile.
25	 *   - `details` — the column beside the image (name/attrs/price/stepper/actions). Figma:
26	 *     gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile.
27	 *   - `info` — the name + colour/size (+ mobile price) block, paired with the desktop-only
28	 *     delivery-actions slot. Figma: column layout desktop / row + justify-space-between
29	 *     mobile. The mobile values match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly
30	 *     (row, space-between, align flex-end) so nothing changes below `md` — only the desktop
31	 *     column switch is new.

34	 * there for different reasons — corrected here (round 2 rework) after reading both chunks
35	 * directly rather than assuming they behave alike:
36	 *   - `Stack` (`chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) passes its own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/
37	 *     `flexDirection`/`gap` as SEPARATE literal props ahead of `{...rest}` in its own render
38	 *     (`jsx(chakra.div, {..., alignItems: align, ..., gap: spacing, ...rest})`). Those land in
39	 *     `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`) `styleProps` tier —
40	 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — which sits ABOVE `__css`, so a
41	 *     `__css`-applied value from this recipe would be silently outranked by Stack's own `gap`
42	 *     whenever this component also sets one. `sx` (last, unconditionally winning) avoids that.
43	 *   - `Flex` (`chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs`) does NOT do the same thing — it does not pass `align`/
44	 *     `justify`/`direction` as separate literal props at all. It bundles all of them into ONE
45	 *     `__css` object, placed BEFORE `{...rest}` (`jsx(chakra.div, {ref, __css: styles, ...rest})`).
46	 *     That is the same silent-full-object-discard mechanism `item-variant.css.ts`'s own docblock
47	 *     documents for `Text` — a later same-named key in one object literal replaces the earlier
48	 *     one, it does not merge — just with the winner reversed: a caller-supplied `__css` prop
49	 *     arriving via `rest` would silently discard Flex's OWN align/justify/direction/etc
50	 *     translation entirely, not the other way around. `sx` is a different prop name, so it never
51	 *     collides with either `__css` at this level — it flows through `rest` untouched and is
52	 *     merged in later, last, by the same `toCSSObject` call. Net effect for this file is
53	 *     unchanged either way: `sx` is safe and correct on both `Flex` and `Stack` here, regardless
54	 *     of which mechanism is in play.

import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * State the component feeds in so this recipe can resolve the Item Details gap widening for an
 * active error-variant ZimmInlineMessage (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Named `hasError` (not
 * e.g. `isError`/`errorActive`) to match the resolution-prop convention already used by every
 * other function-form baseStyle in this codebase — zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts's own `disabled`
 * key, and that file's own comment on why: theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts's
 * PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError,
 * focused, filled}`, so a differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch
 * walked by that guard.
 */
export type ZimmCartItemStyleProps = {
  hasError?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Co-located recipe for the cart line-item shell (overrides/app/components/product-item).
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2) — restyles the copy-first port to the Figma-sourced cart-item spec.
 *
 * Parts:
 *   - `row` — the image + item-details row. Figma: gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align
 *     centre desktop / start mobile.
 *   - `details` — the column beside the image (name/attrs/price/stepper/actions). Figma:
 *     gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile.
 *   - `info` — the name + colour/size (+ mobile price) block, paired with the desktop-only
 *     delivery-actions slot. Figma: column layout desktop / row + justify-space-between
 *     mobile. The mobile values match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly
 *     (row, space-between, align flex-end) so nothing changes below `md` — only the desktop
 *     column switch is new.
 *
 * Applied via `sx`, not `__css`, though the two parts of this file's `Flex`/`Stack` pair get
 * there for different reasons — corrected here (round 2 rework) after reading both chunks
 * directly rather than assuming they behave alike:
 *   - `Stack` (`chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) passes its own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/
 *     `flexDirection`/`gap` as SEPARATE literal props ahead of `{...rest}` in its own render
 *     (`jsx(chakra.div, {..., alignItems: align, ..., gap: spacing, ...rest})`). Those land in
 *     `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`) `styleProps` tier —
 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — which sits ABOVE `__css`, so a
 *     `__css`-applied value from this recipe would be silently outranked by Stack's own `gap`
 *     whenever this component also sets one. `sx` (last, unconditionally winning) avoids that.
 *   - `Flex` (`chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs`) does NOT do the same thing — it does not pass `align`/
 *     `justify`/`direction` as separate literal props at all. It bundles all of them into ONE
 *     `__css` object, placed BEFORE `{...rest}` (`jsx(chakra.div, {ref, __css: styles, ...rest})`).
 *     That is the same silent-full-object-discard mechanism `item-variant.css.ts`'s own docblock
 *     documents for `Text` — a later same-named key in one object literal replaces the earlier
 *     one, it does not merge — just with the winner reversed: a caller-supplied `__css` prop
 *     arriving via `rest` would silently discard Flex's OWN align/justify/direction/etc
 *     translation entirely, not the other way around. `sx` is a different prop name, so it never
 *     collides with either `__css` at this level — it flows through `rest` untouched and is
 *     merged in later, last, by the same `toCSSObject` call. Net effect for this file is
 *     unchanged either way: `sx` is safe and correct on both `Flex` and `Stack` here, regardless
 *     of which mechanism is in play.
 *
 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `details`'s desktop gap now branches on `hasError` — 12px
 * (`var(--zimm-scale-s)`) by default, widening to 16px (`var(--zimm-scale-m)`) when an
 * error-variant ZimmInlineMessage is present, per `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2 ("In error
 * states the Item Details gap widens 12 -> 16px"). Only the desktop step changes — the mobile
 * gap (24px, `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`) is untouched: the design record only calls out the desktop
 * value, and 24px already exceeds 16px, so there is nothing to "widen" on mobile. `baseStyle` is
 * therefore now a function of `hasError` (see `ZimmCartItemStyleProps` above) rather than the
 * plain object it was through SFCC-270 — `row`/`info` are unchanged and simply ignore the new
 * prop.
 */
export const ZimmCartItem = {
  parts: ['row', 'details', 'info'],
  baseStyle: ({ hasError = false }: ZimmCartItemStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    row: {
      flexDirection: 'row',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        alignItems: 'center',
        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px desktop
      },
    },
    details: {
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        // 16px (var(--zimm-scale-m) = foundation/spacing.ts's `m` = 1rem) when an error-variant
        // message is active, else the existing 12px (var(--zimm-scale-s)) — see this file's own
        // docblock and ZimmCartItemStyleProps above.
        gap: hasError ? 'var(--zimm-scale-m)' : 'var(--zimm-scale-s)',
      },
    },
    info: {
      flexDirection: 'row',
      justifyContent: 'space-between',
      alignItems: 'flex-end',
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        flexDirection: 'column',
        alignItems: 'flex-start',
        justifyContent: 'flex-start',
      },
    },
  }),
};

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED } from 'app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared';

/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the value display's dimmed state.
 *  Named `disabled` (not e.g. `isUnavailable`) to match the resolution-prop convention already
 *  used by every other function-form baseStyle in this codebase (zimmTextInput.css.ts's own
 *  `disabled` key) — `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only
 *  exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}`, so a
 *  differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch walked by that guard. */
export type ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps = {
  disabled?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).
 *
 * `root` — the flex row. Gap is 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` — foundation/spacing.ts's `xs` is
 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from
 * Figma's own raw annotation, which shows a 12px gap around a bare 12px glyph with no drawn
 * touch target at all. ZimmButton's `icon` size variant already resolves both buttons to a 24px
 * touch target (zimmButton.css.ts `sizes.icon` — `minW`/`minH`: `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, cited
 * there against WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, and matching the Figma node's own literal name
 * `touchTarget` at value 24) — i.e. 6px of invisible padding is already added on every side of
 * each 12px glyph before this gap is even applied. An 8px authored gap between the two 24px
 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the
 * annotated 12px), without shrinking either button below its accessible 24px target — the
 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,
 * not a straight copy of the raw annotation.
 *
 * `value` — the numeric display. No Figma node or type-style was supplied for this specific text
 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching
 * into an unrelated atom's styling module for the number. Applying the SAME opacity to `root`
 * as well would double it up on the buttons (0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, not 0.4) — deliberately scoped to
 * `value` only for that reason.
 */
export const ZimmQuantityStepper = {
  parts: ['root', 'value'],
  baseStyle: ({ disabled }: ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    root: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
    },
    value: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center',
      textStyle: 'body2Strong',
      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
      opacity: disabled ? OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED : 1,
    },
  }),
};

389	### SFCC-795 — Cart Item UI Part 2 · the largest card
390	
391	Groups: default state (restates 270); stepper states (quantity 1 → `–` disabled/greyed; > 1 → both
392	enabled; at max → `+` disabled/greyed; fully OOS or unavailable → **both** disabled/greyed); error
393	state (red inline message beneath the stepper — OOS, Partially OOS, Unavailable, copy supplied);
394	promotional price ("Was $X" / "Now $Y" replacing standard price, plus a discount label beneath the
395	stepper e.g. "20% off applied"); warning state (grey info icon + message, e.g. "Maximum purchase
396	quantity reached for this size"); responsive; and **11 accessibility ACs**.
397	
398	Decisions:
399	- **Overlap with 270/271/250 is intentional layering — build once, satisfy all.** This is the
400	  explicit reason for bundling. Consequence to accept: the ACs can't be signed off independently and
401	  Zephyr will count the same coverage from three keys.

860	## 11.10 Design open items — RESOLVED (2026-09-16)
861	
862	**(4) `25px` raw value — DECIDED (Marcel): implement 24px** (`--zimm-scale-xl`… actually
863	`space/600`), with a short comment noting the design specified 25 and it was snapped to the nearest
864	tokenised value. Applies to the Item Actions gap and the empty-bag paragraph spacing.
865	
866	**(5) Two token namespaces — RESOLVED from the codebase.** Our `--zimm-font-*` vars mirror
867	`brand/font/*`'s shape (family / size / lineheight / letterspacing), not `default/*` +
868	`line-height/*`. So `brand/font/*` is the current generation; the `default/*` usages (empty-bag
869	body, promo accordion) are the older one.
870	**More useful: our 22 registered textStyles map near 1:1 to the Figma named styles** — map style→
871	textStyle, not var-by-var:
872	`Default/body2`→`body2` · `body2-strong`→`body2Strong` · `Caption`→`caption` ·
873	`Link-sm`→`linkSm` · `Product-name`/`Product Names`→`productNames` · `Price`→`price` ·
874	`Button-lg`→`button` · `Body 1`→`body1` · `Body 2 Medium`→`body2Strong`
875	**Two gaps:** no `captionStrong` for Figma's `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart item's colour+size
876	line, medium/500) — we only have `caption`. And `mobileBody1`/`mobileBody2`/`mobileBody1Strong`
877	exist, so there are mobile-specific styles to consider for the reflow.
878	
879	**(6) Two tokens for #969696 — RESOLVED from the codebase.** We have
880	`text.muted = grey[300] = #969696` and **no `subtlest`**. Both Figma names collapse onto
881	**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
882	**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
883	| Figma | Ours |
884	|---|---|
885	| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
886	| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
887	| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
888	| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
889	| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
890	| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
891	| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |
892	
893	**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
894	state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
895	- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
896	  (regular/400, ls 0)
897	- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
898	  where the gutter should be 32px
899	- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
900	- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
901	Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
902	=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
903	   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.
904	
905	**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
906	("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
907	("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
908	the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
909	**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
910	information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
911	specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.
912	
913	**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
914	- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
915	  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
916	  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the

## 11.10 Design open items — RESOLVED (2026-09-16)

**(4) `25px` raw value — DECIDED (Marcel): implement 24px** (`--zimm-scale-xl`… actually
`space/600`), with a short comment noting the design specified 25 and it was snapped to the nearest
tokenised value. Applies to the Item Actions gap and the empty-bag paragraph spacing.

**(5) Two token namespaces — RESOLVED from the codebase.** Our `--zimm-font-*` vars mirror
`brand/font/*`'s shape (family / size / lineheight / letterspacing), not `default/*` +
`line-height/*`. So `brand/font/*` is the current generation; the `default/*` usages (empty-bag
body, promo accordion) are the older one.
**More useful: our 22 registered textStyles map near 1:1 to the Figma named styles** — map style→
textStyle, not var-by-var:
`Default/body2`→`body2` · `body2-strong`→`body2Strong` · `Caption`→`caption` ·
`Link-sm`→`linkSm` · `Product-name`/`Product Names`→`productNames` · `Price`→`price` ·
`Button-lg`→`button` · `Body 1`→`body1` · `Body 2 Medium`→`body2Strong`
**Two gaps:** no `captionStrong` for Figma's `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart item's colour+size
line, medium/500) — we only have `caption`. And `mobileBody1`/`mobileBody2`/`mobileBody1Strong`
exist, so there are mobile-specific styles to consider for the reflow.

**(6) Two tokens for #969696 — RESOLVED from the codebase.** We have
`text.muted = grey[300] = #969696` and **no `subtlest`**. Both Figma names collapse onto
**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
| Figma | Ours |
|---|---|
| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |

**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
  (regular/400, ls 0)
- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
  where the gutter should be 32px
- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.

**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.

**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the
  mobile cart item image. Same token, different fallback => the decimal is what Figma rendered after
  scaling, not the token value. **Use the token (48 / 40), never the decimal.**
- **Tablet 659.2 is a computed fill width, not a spec.** `659.2 = 595.2 content + 2 × 32 gutter`;
  the gutter is a real token (32px). Confirmed NOT a uniformly scaled instance — the tablet header
  is its own 92px and the message band is exactly 52 (unscaled).
  **Implement tablet as a fluid width with a 32px gutter, never a hardcoded 659.2.**

### Responsive rule (derived)
| | Panel | Layout | Gutter | Header |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 1440+ | **fixed 1186px** | two-column (items 360 / totals 430, 140 gutter) | 128 | 84 |
| Tablet 834 | fluid (~79%) | **single column** | **32** | 92 |
| Mobile 402 | full-width | single column | 32 | 108 (68 in some states — drift) |

### Additional drift found while resolving these
- **The mobile message band hardcodes `px-[128px]` across multiple states** — should be 32px.
  Systematic, not a one-off.
- **Mobile header height varies by state**: 108 (default) vs 68 (error states).
- **Within a single node, one message is `w-full` and the next is `w-[476px]`** (mobile
  warnings-hidden). Clear drift.

## 11.11 Final three design items — SETTLED (Marcel, 2026-09-16). None go to the designer as questions.

10	import {useIntl} from 'react-intl'
11	import {useVariationParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-params'
12	import {useVariationAttributes} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes'
13	import {useSelectedStore} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-selected-store'
14	
15	const OUT_OF_STOCK = 'OUT_OF_STOCK'
16	const UNFULFILLABLE = 'UNFULFILLABLE'
17	
18	const getInventoryById = (product, inventoryId) => {
19	    if (!inventoryId || !product?.inventories) {
20	        return null
21	    }
22	    return product.inventories.find((inv) => inv.id === inventoryId)
23	}
24	
25	// TODO: This needs to be refactored.
26	// If compatibility with API version < v8.1 is needed, keep pickupInStore as false
27	export const useDerivedProduct = (
28	    product,
29	    isProductPartOfSet = false,
30	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
31	    pickupInStore = false,
32	    controlledVariationValues = null,
33	    onVariationChange = null
34	) => {
35	    const showLoading = !product
36	    const isProductABundle = product?.type?.bundle
37	    const stockLevel = product?.inventory?.stockLevel || 0
38	    const stepQuantity = product?.stepQuantity || 1
39	    const minOrderQuantity = stockLevel > 0 ? product?.minOrderQuantity || 1 : 0
40	    const initialQuantity = product?.quantity || product?.minOrderQuantity || 1
41	
42	    // used for product bundles when there are multiple products
43	    const lowestStockLevelProductName = product?.inventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
44	    const intl = useIntl()
45	    const variant = useVariant(
46	        product,
47	        isProductPartOfSet,
48	        isProductPartOfBundle,
49	        controlledVariationValues
50	    )
51	    const isStandardProduct = product?.type?.item
52	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
53	        product,
54	        isProductPartOfSet,
55	        isProductPartOfBundle,
56	        controlledVariationValues
57	    )
58	    const variationAttributes = useVariationAttributes(
59	        product,
60	        isProductPartOfSet,
61	        isProductPartOfBundle,
62	        controlledVariationValues,
63	        onVariationChange
64	    )
65	    const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(initialQuantity)
66	    const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()
67	
68	    // A product is considered out of stock if the stock level is 0 or if we have all our
69	    // variation attributes selected, but don't have a variant. We do this because the API
70	    // will sometimes return all the variants even if they are out of stock, but for other
71	    // products it won't.
72	    const isOutOfStock =
73	        !stockLevel ||
74	        (!isProductABundle &&
75	            !variant &&
76	            !isStandardProduct &&
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).length === variationAttributes.length) ||
78	        (!isProductABundle && variant && !variant.orderable)
79	    const unfulfillable = stockLevel < quantity
80	
81	    // Product details for selected store
82	    const selectedStoreInventory = getInventoryById(product, selectedStore?.inventoryId)
83	    const selectedStoreStockLevel = selectedStoreInventory?.stockLevel || 0
84	    const selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName =
85	        selectedStoreInventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
86	    // selectedStoreStockLevel and selectedStoreInventory are already variant specific,
87	    // so we don't need to check for variation attributes
88	    const isSelectedStoreOutOfStock = !selectedStoreStockLevel || !selectedStoreInventory?.orderable
89	    const selectedStoreUnfulfillable = selectedStoreStockLevel < quantity
90	
91	    // Use appropriate inventory based on pickup/delivery selection
92	    const currentStockLevel = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreStockLevel : stockLevel
93	    const currentLowestStockLevelProductName = pickupInStore
94	        ? selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName
95	        : lowestStockLevelProductName
96	    const currentIsOutOfStock = pickupInStore ? isSelectedStoreOutOfStock : isOutOfStock
97	    const currentUnfulfillable = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreUnfulfillable : unfulfillable
98	
99	    const inventoryMessages = {
100	        [OUT_OF_STOCK]: intl.formatMessage({
101	            defaultMessage: 'Out of stock',
102	            id: 'use_product.message.out_of_stock'
103	        }),
104	        [UNFULFILLABLE]: currentLowestStockLevelProductName
105	            ? intl.formatMessage(
106	                  {
107	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left for {productName}!',
108	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining_for_product'
109	                  },
110	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel, productName: currentLowestStockLevelProductName}
111	              )
112	            : intl.formatMessage(
113	                  {
114	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left!',
115	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining'
116	                  },
117	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel}
118	              )
119	    }
120	
121	    // showInventoryMessage controls if add to cart button is disabled
122	    const showInventoryMessage =
123	        (variant || isProductABundle || isStandardProduct) &&
124	        (currentIsOutOfStock || currentUnfulfillable)
125	    const inventoryMessage =
126	        (currentIsOutOfStock && inventoryMessages[OUT_OF_STOCK]) ||
127	        (currentUnfulfillable && inventoryMessages[UNFULFILLABLE])
128	
129	    // If the `initialQuantity` changes, update the state. This typically happens
130	    // when either the master product changes, or the inventory of the product changes
131	    // from out-of-stock to in-stock or vice versa.
132	    useEffect(() => {
133	        setQuantity(initialQuantity)
134	    }, [initialQuantity])
135	
136	    // Lump the out of stock/unfulfillable checks together for easier consumption
137	    return {
138	        showLoading,
139	        showInventoryMessage,
140	        inventoryMessage,
141	        variationAttributes,
142	        quantity,
143	        minOrderQuantity,
144	        stepQuantity,
145	        variationParams,
146	        setQuantity,
147	        variant,
148	        stockLevel,
149	        isOutOfStock,
150	        unfulfillable,
151	        isSelectedStoreOutOfStock: isSelectedStoreOutOfStock || selectedStoreUnfulfillable,
152	        selectedStore
153	    }
154	}
